implementation_notes: The owner holds std::unordered_map<std::string, std::any>: std::any is a type-safe container for single values of any copy-constructible type and any_cast is the checked read, which replaces the classic void* property slot. Descriptors stay explicit - an enum or key table plus the type each key must hold - because a wrong-type read only fails when any_cast is used; where the legal value set is closed, std::variant makes it part of the type instead of runtime metadata. The classic structure is hand-written because C++ has no reflective member lookup.
pitfalls: std::any stores only copy-constructible types and any_cast<T> on the wrong alternative throws std::bad_any_cast - read through the pointer overload and report absence and type errors instead of exceptions.
Keys and values are per instance: every property costs a std::string plus (usually) an allocation inside the any, so for small objects a flat vector of pairs or an enum-keyed std::variant is cheaper.
No standard container is thread-safe: concurrent set/get on the same map is a data race even when writers only insert new keys, and a rehash invalidates iterators held by readers.

variants.name: Boost dynamic property maps (library)
variants.implementation_notes: Boost's dynamic property maps collect heterogeneous property maps and address them by string key - each property map is assigned a string-based key when it is added to the collection, and get/put convert key and value at run time, signalling property_not_found, dynamic_get_failure or a bad_any_cast instead of returning an empty value. Choose it when the named properties already exist as Boost property maps (graphs, algorithms) or must be shared across several containers; prefer the std::any map when only one object's attributes are meant.
pitfalls: Type mismatches surface as boost::bad_any_cast or dynamic_get_failure exceptions at run time, and the underlying maps must outlive the dynamic_properties collection.
It is a runtime view over statically typed maps: the same name can address different maps for different key types, so readers and writers must agree on the key type.
